name: 2011 Prairie Avenue — Romanesque neighbour of Mayer (district draft; refined by T-1915)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B brick dwelling with a stone front and a rounded corner bay (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2352, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1915 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2011-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2011-front, s35-2011-wing) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-076 (Romanesque neighbour of Mayer); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 2011 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2011 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 20.000, v -3.755 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.383 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front), widened to 5.5 m along the front because the fitted strip was narrower than any house of the avenue (T-2690). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '2½B; rear2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 2 full storeys and a half storey in the roof.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick with stone front'.

Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Romanesque' overlaid with the frontage row: The Romanesque neighbour of Mayer (the Lambs' in the 1904 Blue Book): the register's 'rough ashlar front, round-arched entrance, rounded corner turret/conical cap' as the Romanesque family's steep hip with dormers over the 2½B body, and a turret under a cone on the south front corner, where the sheet draws its stone rounded bay. Seen in the 1890s Mayer photograph; T-1915 reads it. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 2468133561 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352.
